ratingBasis: Editorial hypotheses based on the current user/workflow catalog and synthetic acceptance stories. No usage-frequency study or source-feasibility verification has been performed.

impact.high: A practical decision still requires repeated ad hoc reconstruction because the current contract lacks the relevant typed domain vocabulary or relationship meaning; the proposal directly removes that gap.
impact.medium: The current contract supports much of the core answer; the proposal adds useful typed fields, interpretation, grouping or presentation.
impact.low: No substantial additional model is justified for the current question: reuse largely covers it, or the proposal is specialized detail without a demonstrated near-term gap.

repeatUse.frequent: Hypothesized to recur in the named workflow across routine deliveries or many relevant objects; not a measured frequency.
repeatUse.occasional: Needed at selected project stages or for a narrower subset of the named workflow.
repeatUse.rare: Only a specialized situation is currently identified.

scopeCost.small: A bounded schedule or field group can be reviewed with one straightforward example.
scopeCost.medium: Several relationships, conventions or incomplete-data cases need joint review.
scopeCost.large: Requires substantial domain rules, new external inputs, topology, time series or difficult geometry.

evidenceBasis.workflow_scenario: The question is grounded in a current worked workflow scenario. This does not validate the proposed record, real source mapping or market demand.
evidenceBasis.brainstorm: An explicit hypothesis suggested by a role or broader workflow; obtain an acceptance example before promotion.

guardrails: Do not rank by number of class names, role tags or workflow links; broad tagging is not evidence of value.
Scope cost does not reduce value. A valuable but difficult capability may need investigation instead of immediate implementation.
Infrequent high-consequence safety or accessibility work requires explicit review; the frequency rule alone must not dismiss it.
A first design wave must cover contrasting workflow families and trades, not only the easiest architectural examples.
A candidate needs an explicit question, decision, grain, minimum fields and separation rationale. A noun alone does not qualify.
Promote a separate record only when stable row meaning, distinct fields or relationships, and a useful query justify it; prefer a subtype label, shared facet or view otherwise.
Design-now is a bounded semantic design experiment, not authorization to generate all candidate classes or claim source feasibility.
Source readiness and derivation cost remain unverified until bounded BOS inspection; empty exports must not decide whether a domain concept matters.
Evaluate incremental model value against the existing contract, not the importance of a profession or workflow. Explicitly record reuse or extension before proposing another record.
promotionChecks: Walk through one named user's decision using the proposed record; compare it with the existing generic representation.
Create a complete and an incomplete example, including the most likely double-counting or wrong-relationship trap.
Explain why existing records plus a label, facet or view do not suffice.
Review stable field meanings, units, spatial scope, identity and external requirements.
Trace at least one actual source-backed example or document an explicit mapping/external-input gap before claiming population support.
Review the SQL/table and C# result shape together; add a row schema only after the candidate passes the semantic review.

activeDesign.whyNow: Provides a recognizable shared context for architectural schedules, finishes, services and handover without classes for each room use.
activeDesign.acceptanceQuestion: Can we give a room-based work list when some spaces are only scheduled, their enclosure is unknown, and services or finishes have no resolved room?

activeDesign.whyNow: A worked shared-wall example already exposes the correct measurement grain. Start from finish_schedule and test whether it can serve the domain directly before creating another record.
activeDesign.acceptanceQuestion: Can painters, flooring and ceiling trades share a finish-face model that preserves partitions, unknown areas and unassigned spaces without counting the host twice?

activeDesign.whyNow: Adds a cross-trade coordination case beyond familiar component schedules: a host opening, several passing services and independent approval/firestop evidence. Doors already have a bounded audit projection to refine later.
activeDesign.acceptanceQuestion: Can the contractor identify which service penetrations need approval or firestop evidence before closing a wall, without inferring ratings or approvals from object names?

activeDesign.whyNow: Adds structural trade requirements early and tests where beams, columns and braces can share stable fields without importing an analytical structural hierarchy.
activeDesign.acceptanceQuestion: Can a fabricator group members by section and material and use measured lengths without substituting bounding-box dimensions or counting analytical duplicates?

activeDesign.whyNow: Electrical schedules need distinct supply and circuit concepts that the generic component model cannot make discoverable. This deliberately tests a discipline beyond architectural takeoff.
activeDesign.acceptanceQuestion: Can an electrician inspect panel and circuit assignments while unknown phases, capacity and upstream connections remain explicit?

activeDesign.whyNow: Tests a useful practical family containing toilets and basins, with real connection and water-use differences, instead of one class for every fixture label.
activeDesign.acceptanceQuestion: Can a plumber produce a per-space fixture and connection schedule without treating missing waste/supply ports as absent services or mixing water-use bases?

activeDesign.whyNow: Tests a concrete mechanical model and prevents shared routing geometry from turning into a universal pipe/duct/tray record. Compare with the pipe candidate before approving the shared facet.
activeDesign.acceptanceQuestion: Can a mechanical trade query duct size, construction, lining and airflow separately from geometry and distinguish an unobserved connection from a disconnected route?

activeDesign.whyNow: Adds delivery and field-audit needs to the first wave. It tests the distinction between what a model specifies and what independent evidence says was delivered or installed.
activeDesign.acceptanceQuestion: Can a project manager reconcile specified items with partial deliveries and repeated observations without treating a modeled object as proof of installation?

existingContractReview.incrementalGain: A typed space view would add room number, use, measured area and enclosure meaning over shared object identity; it must not create another identity.
Extend existing door audit projection with scope/operation/space concepts only where a new question requires them.
Extend assembly or edge details after testing the gap; reuse existing area selection and occurrence identity.
Test whether the existing face record can serve the domain after clearer naming; add partition/specification detail only if required.
Compose inventory and handover coverage from existing concepts; specialized equipment fields belong in concrete models or justified facets.
Compose room-based procurement/context without a second identity or finish measurement store.
Expose selected quantities and missing coverage through a view; preserve the original observations.
Existing package scope is sufficient for the worked estimate; release/dependency fields remain an incremental design question.
Use existing impact grain and factor context; test aggregate coverage rather than creating another result fact.
The existing assessment record already has the requested grain and incomplete outcomes.
Add typed section/material/axis relationships for physical member schedules; reuse object identity and quantity evidence.
Add electrical supply and circuit vocabulary absent from generic component/edge rows.
Add fixture role and explicit supply/waste and water-use bases, retaining shared physical identity.
Add duct construction, lining, dimensions and airflow vocabulary; geometry and adjacency alone cannot express it.
Add pipe material, size and conditional slope/pressure context; share geometry without forcing duct semantics.
Add the host-opening/passing-service/approval association and distinguish required from observed firestop evidence.
Independent delivery or installation events need a subject, event scope and evidence grain separate from the modeled occurrence.

scenarioSupport.supports: Stable room references let opposite wall faces carry separate finish quantities.
scenarioSupport.doesNotEstablish: Space enclosure, occupancy and room-area definitions.

scenarioSupport.supports: Missing width/rating evidence prevents a complete audit.
scenarioSupport.doesNotEstablish: Door operation, leaf-versus-assembly rules and connected-space topology.

scenarioSupport.supports: One physical wall can have two separately measured finishes.
scenarioSupport.doesNotEstablish: Wall construction layers, loadbearing role and complete opening deductions.

scenarioSupport.supports: Net surface, projected area, competing observations and unmeasured scope differ.
scenarioSupport.doesNotEstablish: Layer ordering, roof drainage and edge details.

scenarioSupport.supports: Face identity prevents host-based finish double counting.
scenarioSupport.doesNotEstablish: All finish partition rules or product specifications.

scenarioSupport.supports: A maintainable asset stays visible despite missing handover data.
scenarioSupport.doesNotEstablish: Pump/head curves, air-handler duties or generic equipment performance fields.

scenarioSupport.supports: Accepted service edges differ from candidate proximity edges.
scenarioSupport.doesNotEstablish: Physical segmentation boundaries, duct construction or pipe pressure semantics.

scenarioSupport.supports: A material contribution must be counted once across source representations.
scenarioSupport.doesNotEstablish: Ordered assembly layers or a general assembly taxonomy.

scenarioSupport.supports: Select a measurement basis and retain unknown scope.
scenarioSupport.doesNotEstablish: Every trade measurement convention or aggregation denominator.

scenarioSupport.supports: An estimate can price known package scope while preserving unpriced scope.
scenarioSupport.doesNotEstablish: Schedule dependencies, release rules or installation progress.

scenarioSupport.supports: Missing manuals are a handover gap rather than absence of an asset.
scenarioSupport.doesNotEstablish: Maintenance intervals, access envelopes or service procedures.

scenarioSupport.supports: Contribution identity and module/factor context constrain an impact line.
scenarioSupport.doesNotEstablish: Full portfolio aggregation, lifecycle completeness or ecological-impact methods.
Any regulatory rule implementation or complete compliance claim.

scenarioSupport.supports: Incomplete inputs must remain visible rather than produce a pass.
scenarioSupport.doesNotEstablish: A comprehensive model-quality rule set or root-cause diagnosis.
